subject: Archaeology
title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Dead Sea Scrolls.

hook.text: In 1947, a Bedouin shepherd threw a rock into a cave and heard a clay jar shatter. Inside were ancient scrolls.

buildup.text: The scrolls contained the oldest known copies of Hebrew Bible texts, dating back over 2,000 years.

discovery.text: Over 900 manuscripts were found in 11 caves near the Dead Sea, written between 250 BCE and 68 CE.

twist.text: Some scrolls were sold on the antiquities black market before scholars even knew they existed.

climax.text: The scrolls showed that biblical texts had been copied with astonishing accuracy for two millennia.

punchline.text: A thrown rock revealed the oldest Bible texts ever found.

quiz.question: How were the Dead Sea Scrolls discovered?
options: A team of archaeologists located them using ground-penetrating radar
A Bedouin shepherd accidentally found them in a cave
They were hidden in a temple and found during renovation

details.summary: The Dead Sea Scrolls, discovered between 1947 and 1956 in caves near Qumran, are the oldest known biblical manuscripts — dating from the 3rd century BCE to the 1st century CE. They include every Old Testament book except Esther, plus sectarian texts revealing a radical Jewish community.
details.whyItMatters: The scrolls pushed the earliest biblical manuscripts back by a thousand years, showing remarkable textual stability. They also revealed the diversity of Judaism before the Temple's destruction, transforming biblical and religious scholarship.
takeaways: Oldest known biblical manuscripts from 3rd century BCE to 1st century CE
Discovered in caves near Qumran between 1947 and 1956
They transformed understanding of ancient Judaism and biblical history

faq.question: How were the Dead Sea Scrolls discovered?
faq.answer: A Bedouin shepherd found the first scrolls in 1947 while searching for a lost goat in a cave near the Dead Sea. Subsequent systematic searches of nearby caves between 1947 and 1956 yielded over 900 manuscripts in various states of preservation.

faq.question: What do the scrolls tell us about the Bible?
faq.answer: Comparing scroll texts to the later Masoretic text shows remarkable stability over a thousand years, with mostly minor variations. However, some scrolls preserve textual variants that differ significantly, suggesting biblical texts were more fluid before standardization than previously thought.
